## PR description
### [Diffusion] Add Worker contracts and RPC plumbing for Scheduler-managed paged KV cache  [labels: merge-test, core, refactor]
## Purpose

This PR adds the Worker-facing request DTO and RPC plumbing for Scheduler-managed diffusion KV cache. It is the W0 follow-up to merged PR #5541 and the W0 control-plane slice of [RFC #5244](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/5244).


The scope is intentionally narrow: this PR defines how a Scheduler allocation snapshot can travel with a newly scheduled diffusion request, while preserving the existing dense execution path. It does not yet create the Scheduler allocator, initialize physical KV pages, install Worker BlockTables, or consume the block IDs in model attention.

## Ownership and data flow

PR #5541 introduced Scheduler-owned logical KV state:

```text
DiffusionKVRequest / DiffusionKVContext
  owner: SchedulerRequestState
  lifetime: mutable across scheduling and native KVCacheManager operations
  rule: never sent to a Worker
```

This PR introduces the corresponding request-time wire snapshot:

```text
DiffusionKVMetadata
  owner: one newly scheduled request envelope
  lifetime: one allocation snapshot
  contents: allocation generation, sequence/context logical bounds,
            native cache-group block IDs
```

The transport path is:

```text
[W1 Scheduler allocation producer]
  -> DiffusionKVMetadata
  -> NewRequestData.diffusion_kv_metadata
  -> MultiprocDiffusionExecutor
       request mode: optional fourth execute_model argument
       batch/step: metadata remains inside DiffusionSchedulerOutput
  -> Diffusion Worker / ModelRunner boundary
  -> [W1 native BlockTable installer]
```

`request.prepared_layout` remains a separate model-owned Worker payload. The generic KV transport does not derive block IDs from it and does not send mutable `DiffusionKVRequest` objects to Workers.

## W0 capability boundary

Metadata is optional in this PR.

Merged PR #5541 stores authoritative `DiffusionKVRequest` objects in `SchedulerRequestState`, removes them from the request sent to the Worker, and does not yet allocate blocks or produce `DiffusionKVMetadata`. Requiring metadata before those producer/installer capabilities exist would make `paged_scheduler` unusable or require fabricated block allocations.

W0 therefore treats these dataclasses as trusted internal DTOs and performs only checks backed by information available at the current execution boundary:

- dense mode rejects unexpected diffusion KV metadata;
- paged mode accepts metadata when supplied but does not require it yet;
- the new-request envelope ID, forwarded request ID, and metadata request ID must agree before model work;
- the historical dense request RPC keeps its existing positional shape.

## Validation ownership

This PR deliberately does not claim strict sequence, cache-group, block-count, or block-range validation. Those checks require independent authoritative state that W0 does not have.

The W1 control-plane and BlockTable follow-up owns these checks at the following boundaries:

```text
Scheduler metadata construction
  -> compare the exact sequence/context set with
     SchedulerRequestState.diffusion_kv_requests
  -> validate sequence IDs, context IDs/roles, and logical lengths

Worker allocation installation
  -> compare cache-group order/count with rank-local native KVCacheConfig
  -> validate required block-table lengths and block ID ranges

Worker allocation registry
  -> enforce allocation_generation idempotency
  -> reject stale or conflicting active snapshots
```

This placement avoids duplicating native `KVCacheConfig`/BlockTable invariants inside a transport DTO and avoids treating DTO-local checks as proof that an allocation matches Scheduler state.

## Main changes

- Add `DiffusionKVContextMetadata`, `DiffusionKVSequenceMetadata`, and  `DiffusionKVMetadata` request allocation DTOs.
- Add optional `diffusion_kv_metadata` to `NewRequestData` so the request and its allocation snapshot cross the Scheduler/Worker boundary atomically …[clipped]
